value: Anne is tall.

Her expressive face and luminous eyes change dynamically with her laughter and imaginative dreams.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, but became an orphan in early infancy. She was raised in hard circumstances by Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond before being placed in an asylum. At eleven years old, she was brought to Avonlea when Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables decided to adopt a child. Though they had originally requested a boy, they chose to keep Anne, who quickly won their affection and formed a deep bond with Matthew as a kindred spirit. She swore eternal friendship with her neighbor Diana Barry and began attending Avonlea school. After schoolmate Gilbert Blythe teased her about her red hair, Anne harbored a intense grudge and engaged in a fierce academic rivalry with him for years. Over time, Anne's vivid imagination led her into various scrapes, including accidentally flavoring a cake with liniment, walking a roof ridgepole on a dare and breaking her ankle, and accidentally dying her hair green. She attended Queen's Academy, where she won the prestigious Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's death and Marilla's failing eyesight, Anne chose to remain at Green Gables to care for Marilla rather than attend college immediately, taking up the position of schoolteacher at Avonlea School. As teacher, she helped form the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and took on a leadership role in community affairs alongside Gilbert, with whom she reconciled and became close friends.

label: History
value: Anthony was taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye
unit: After being taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye and her husband, Anthony began attending the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. From the beginning, he held a hostile attitude toward Anne, expressing the belief that she was no good simply because she was a female teacher. He frequently caused minor trouble in school, such as pouring water from his slate bottle down Aurelia Clay's neck, remaining unmoved when kept in at recess for a talk about how gentlemen should behave. On another occasion, he placed a live mouse inside Anne's desk drawer to startle her. When Anne caught him mocking her, she punished him with a pointer until his bravado broke and tears came to his eyes.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman is nicknamed Charlotta the Fourth.
unit: Leonora Bowman, nicknamed Charlotta the Fourth, came to live at Echo Lodge as a handmaiden to Miss Lavendar Lewis, following in the footsteps of her three older sisters. She served her mistress with great devotion, keeping her secrets, tending the garden, and assisting around the house. When visitors like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry came to Echo Lodge, Charlotta greeted them warmly for the sake of her mistress. She assisted with sewing Miss Lavendar's organdy dress and expressed genuine concern to Anne when Miss Lavendar seemed out of spirits. Before Miss Lavendar's wedding, Charlotta threw herself enthusiastically into helping Anne and Diana prepare the stone house for the event.

Davy began attending school alongside his sister, sharing a desk with Milty Boulter and frequently making terrible faces at Paul Irving. He also spent time helping Mr. Harrison haul dulse and assisting John Henry Carter in executing two white roosters. Over time, under Anne's gentle guidance, Davy's behavior reformed significantly.

After his mother passed away, Davy and his twin sister Dora were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Shortly after his arrival, Davy grew devoted to Anne Shirley and strove to wash his face regularly to win her approval over Paul Irving. He frequently got into trouble due to his boundless curiosity and mischievous nature, such as hanging over the well to find where the dark went or being sent upstairs by Marilla for disobedience. Davy began attending school alongside his sister, sharing a desk with Milty Boulter and frequently making terrible faces at Paul Irving. He also spent time helping Mr. Harrison haul dulse and assisting John Henry Carter in executing two white roosters. Over time, under Anne's gentle guidance, Davy's behavior reformed significantly.

label: History
value: Diana grows up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana grows up at Orchard Slope and meets Anne Shirley when Anne comes to Green Gables. The two swear eternal bosom friendship by a brook, spending their childhood playing in spots like Idlewild and Willowmere, creating a story club, and attending Avonlea school together. After accidentally getting drunk on Marilla's currant wine, Diana is briefly forbidden by her strict mother from playing with Anne, but they are reconciled after Anne helps cure her little sister Minnie May of severe croup. She sings a solo at the Avonlea hall concert and later visits Charlottetown with Anne and her father. Though her parents decide against sending her to Queen's Academy, she maintains her deep bond with Anne. Later, Diana becomes treasurer of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, joins in group outings to places like Echo Lodge, and eventually becomes engaged to Fred Wright.

label: History
value: Dora was raised by Mary Joe.
unit: Dora was raised by her sickly mother, Mary Joe, alongside her twin brother Davy until their mother's passing. Marilla Cuthbert brought the twins to live at Green Gables, where Dora quickly fit in as a helpful and remarkably composed child who assisted with household chores such as wiping dishes, picking peas, and feeding chickens. When she started attending school, she was initially seated with Mirabel Cotton. label: History
value: Gilbert spent three years in Alberta with his sick father.
unit: After spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and visiting cousins in New Brunswick, Gilbert returned to school in Avonlea. He quickly established an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley while attempting to make amends for teasing her. At Queen's Academy, he took the Second Year course to earn a First Class teacher's license in a single year and emerged as one of the top medal contestants. Because his father could not afford college right away, Gilbert took up teaching at White Sands to earn his tuition, selflessly surrendering the Avonlea school position to Anne so she could stay at Green Gables. He served as president of the newly formed Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne and their friends. After completing his teaching term at White Sands and resigning his position, he prepared to leave for Redmond College alongside Anne to study to become a doctor.

label: History
value: Mr. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Mr. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his sister kept house for him until her death. Before she died, he promised her he would marry Emily Scott. Upon marrying Emily, their opposing habits led to constant friction, particularly over his grammar, smoking, and his attachment to his deceased brother's swearing parrot, Ginger. The couple parted ways after a quarrel over the bird, and Mr. Harrison left New Brunswick to buy Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island. In Avonlea, he lived as a bachelor, hired John Henry Carter, and quickly developed a reputation as an outspoken crank. He initially clashed with Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow, but they soon became good friends. Eventually, following Ginger's death, Emily tracked him down in Avonlea and reconciled with him. With his wife's return, Mr. Harrison's household settled down, and he began attending church regularly.

label: History
value: Jane attended school in Avonlea.
unit: Jane attended school in Avonlea, where she prepared a dialogue with Ruby Gillis and Diana Barry under Miss Stacy, and studied for the Entrance examination to Queen's Academy. Despite insisting she would not shed a tear when their teacher Mr. Phillips left, she wept so hard she had to borrow her brother's handkerchief. She passed her exams and attended Queen's Academy, taking the Second Class course and taking top honors in domestic science. After graduating, she accepted a teaching post in Newbridge, earning a place on the School Inspector's Roll of Honor. Outside of teaching, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, chaired a committee to raise funds to paint the hall, and helped canvass local residents.

label: History
value: Josie Pye attended Avonlea school.
unit: Josie Pye attended Avonlea school, where she once peeped in her book during a spelling class. During a game of dares with her schoolmates, she successfully walked the Barrys' board fence with airy unconcern after Anne Shirley dared her. When preparing for a school concert, she was sulky because she did not get the role of the fairy queen in a dialogue. At the Exhibition, she earned first prize for her knitted lace. She joined the Queen's class, stating she was going to college for education's sake because she would not have to earn her own living. While at Queen's Academy, she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student. She was the final member of the Pye family to pass through the Avonlea school.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge
unit: Miss Lavendar lived at Echo Lodge in Grafton for many years in quiet seclusion after a youthful quarrel parted her from her fiancé, Stephen Irving. Because she could not afford grown servants after her mother passed away, she adopted a system of hiring young girls for board and clothes, calling each of them "Charlotta" to avoid confusion. In her mid-forties, she met Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, developing a warm friendship with Anne as a kindred spirit. Through Anne's introduction of young Paul Irving, Stephen Irving learned of Miss Lavendar's unmarried status and returned to court her. The two reconciled, leading to a simple wedding ceremony held in the honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with her brother Matthew into her sixties. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help Matthew on the farm, they were mistakenly sent a young girl named Anne Shirley. Though initially intent on returning Anne, Marilla was moved to keep her after witnessing Mrs. Blewett's harsh nature. Over the following years, Marilla raised Anne with strict discipline, aiming to form her into a sensible girl while secretly growing deeply attached to her. When Matthew died suddenly, Marilla confessed her deep affection to Anne. As Marilla began suffering severe eye pain that impaired her reading and sewing, she stepped up to manage the farm responsibilities. Following the death of a distant relative, Mary Keith, Marilla took in Mary's orphaned six-year-old twins, Davy and Dora, taking full charge of raising them at Green Gables with Anne's help.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. In his sixties, troubled by heart problems and needing help with farm work, he agreed with Marilla to adopt a boy from an asylum. Upon driving to Bright River station, he met Anne Shirley instead due to a mistake. Despite his lifelong dread of little girls, Matthew was immediately charmed by Anne's chatter and advocated keeping her at Green Gables. Over the following years, he became Anne's devoted friend and spoiled her, even braving his shyness to get her a fashionable puffed-sleeve dress and organdy gowns. His heart spells grew more frequent, requiring him to avoid excitement and heavy labor. Shortly after Anne completed her Queen's exam studies, Matthew read a newspaper report about the failure of the Abbey Bank, suffered a fatal sudden shock, and died instantly on the porch threshold. He was buried in Avonlea, where Anne continued visiting his grave weekly.

unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. In his sixties, troubled by heart problems and needing help with farm work, he agreed with Marilla to adopt a boy from an asylum. Upon driving to Bright River station, he met Anne Shirley instead due to a mistake. Despite his lifelong dread of little girls, Matthew was immediately charmed by Anne's chatter and advocated keeping her at Green Gables. Over the following years, he became Anne's devoted friend and spoiled her, even braving his shyness to get her a fashionable puffed-sleeve dress and organdy gowns. His heart spells grew more frequent, requiring him to avoid excitement and heavy labor. Shortly after Anne completed her Queen's exam studies, Matthew read a newspaper report about the failure of the Abbey Bank, suffered a fatal sudden shock, and died instantly on the porch threshold. He was buried in Avonlea, where Anne continued visiting his grave weekly.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from Boston
unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Avonlea. On his first day attending Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond of friendship and mutual understanding with his teacher, Anne Shirley. He established himself as an outstanding, popular pupil, even winning over local skeptics like Rachel Lynde despite his American background. Paul engaged in a drawn battle with fellow student St. Clair Donnell to defend the honor of the Stars and Stripes, leading to mutual respect between the two. He also developed a childhood crush on Gracie Andrews, once ducking his head into a spring to prove his hair was naturally curly when teased. When Anne resigned her teaching position to attend college, Paul was deeply heartbroken. Later, his father Stephen Irving arrived unexpectedly to visit, leading to a joyful reunion and Stephen's eventual reconciliation with Miss Lavendar Lewis.

unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Avonlea. On his first day attending Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond of friendship and mutual understanding with his teacher, Anne Shirley. He established himself as an outstanding, popular pupil, even winning over local skeptics like Rachel Lynde despite his American background. Paul engaged in a drawn battle with fellow student St. Clair Donnell to defend the honor of the Stars and Stripes, leading to mutual respect between the two. He also developed a childhood crush on Gracie Andrews, once ducking his head into a spring to prove his hair was naturally curly when teased. When Anne resigned her teaching position to attend college, Paul was deeply heartbroken. Later, his father Stephen Irving arrived unexpectedly to visit, leading to a joyful reunion and Stephen's eventual reconciliation with Miss Lavendar Lewis.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips taught at the Avonlea school
unit: Mr. Phillips taught at the Avonlea school, where he boarded at Eben Wright's house. During his time as master, he was known for spending most of his attention preparing his older students for Queen's and neglecting the younger pupils. On one occasion, he embarrassed Anne Shirley on her first day by holding up her marked slate before the class, and later made her stand on the platform by the blackboard after a fit of temper. He also got into a dispute with Sam Boulter's father after whipping Sam for talk in class. Mr. Phillips spent considerable time courting Prissy Andrews, hearing her Latin lessons in the back of the room and giving her Mayflowers.

label: History
value: Priscilla attended Queen's Academy.
unit: While attending Queen's Academy, Priscilla formed a close circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. She was initially assigned to teach at Carmody school, though she later took her home school instead. She joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and read a paper on cemeteries for one of their meetings. During a spring visit, she joined Anne, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews on a woodland walk. While her aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, was visiting the Island, Priscilla brought her and Mrs. Pendexter to visit Green Gables unexpectedly to surprise Anne.

label: Personality
value: Rachel Lynde is a capable woman.
unit: Rachel Lynde is a capable, outspoken, and highly opinionated woman who prides herself on always speaking her mind. She is a busybody who keeps a sharp eye on everyone's business and dearly loves to give advice. Though she can be sharp, critical, and easily shocked by naughtiness, she is fundamentally a kind, good-hearted woman and a tender nurse. She is also a passionate, red-hot politician, a firm believer in predestination, and holds strong prejudices against outsiders.

label: History
value: Rachel Lynde lived for decades with her husband Thomas at Lynde's Hollow in Avonleta.
unit: Rachel Lynde lived for decades with her husband Thomas at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, managing her household and dominating local church societies while keeping close tabs on all neighborhood events. When Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel visited Green Gables and insulted Anne's looks, prompting a fiery outburst from the girl; however, she readily accepted Anne's apology and eventually grew very fond of her. Being an ardent Liberal, she traveled to Charlottetown with Marilla and Thomas to attend a political mass meeting. At the local exhibition, she won first prize for her butter and cheese. Over time, her husband Thomas fell ill and eventually passed away quiet and unobtrusively, leaving Rachel grieving and facing financial difficulties because the farm had been mortgaged to help their youngest son in the West. Unable to keep the farm, she made arrangements to sell her extra household goods and accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, setting up her quarters in the spare room.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as Avonlea's first female teacher. Upon taking charge of Avonlea school, she introduced innovative methods such as morning and evening physical culture exercises, biweekly Friday recitation afternoons, and field days dedicated to studying flowers, ferns, and birds. She formed the Queen's class to prepare ambitious pupils for the Entrance examinations to Queen's Academy, advising students like Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe on their academic tracks. During her tenure, she gently corrected student missteps—such as Anne reading novels in class—and held mock practice exams in June. Her term in Avonlea concluded at the end of the school year, marked by a touching farewell to her students. She later revisited Avonlea, where she was invited to attend a dinner held by Anne Shirley in honor of visiting author Mrs. Morgan.
